Hello Yuns,
Following recent issues identified with the CCS plug, please find below the summarized root causes, troubleshooting steps, and required actions:
Root Causes Identified
Water ingress on CCS plug leading to incorrect CP (Control Pilot) readings –
Hardware issue.
Corrosion observed on connector blades.
Inspection & Action Steps
Visual Inspection
Perform a visual check of the CCS plug for signs of corrosion or water ingress.
Do not unmount the plug
to preserve eligibility for warranty claims with Phoenix.
CP Pin Voltage Check
Instruct the RC to measure voltage between the CP pin and ground.
If the voltage is
not a constant 12V DC
, the cable must be replaced.
Report all findings in the ticket.
Cable Return Instructions
If replacement is necessary, ship the cable back to QM and include:
Charger Serial Number
Outlet Number and Position (e.g., DC1 – Left)
Cable lifetime (from commissioning to replacement)
If Voltage is Correct
Remove and reinsert the cables securely.
Monitor the system for any improvement.
If the issue persists (e.g., 15ºC temperature difference remains), proceed with cable replacement.
MLFB NO-
